content.todaysFocus: Week 6 is the first sustainable inflection point: crying is at or just past peak, and a daily daylight stroller loop now does triple duty for Avi's sensory input, Anoushka's cardiovascular recovery, and the household's routine.

actionItems.body: Walk a 20-30 minute daylight stroller loop most days. It delivers varied sensory input for Avi, supports Anoushka's gradual return to activity, and resets the afternoon for everyone.
Keep giving Avi 400 IU/day of vitamin D if he is exclusively or predominantly breastfed. Sun exposure on a stroller walk does not replace the supplement, since infants should stay out of direct sun.
Confirm Avi's 2-month well visit is booked. The window is day 56-70, and the first rotavirus dose must be given by roughly day 104, so do not let it slip much past day 70.

watchFors: [low concern] Hiccups during or after feeds, wet sneezing, and a quiet startle on loud sounds are all normal this week.
[monitor] No social smile yet. Many infants smile by now, but flag it at the 2-month visit if it has not appeared by 8 weeks.
[call within 24h] A cluster of new symptoms together, such as poor feeding plus lethargy plus a clear drop in wet diapers.
[call now] Rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher in an infant under 3 months, blue color around the lips, or labored breathing. For blue lips or an unresponsive episode, call 911 now!

enrichment.body: Sing a slow walking tune live during the stroller loop, varying the genre day to day. Live serve-and-return singing, not recorded audio, is the active ingredient for early auditory and language development.
Bring one board book and read a couple of pages on a bench stop. Daily shared reading builds the pre-literacy foundation pediatricians now treat as a routine prescription.
Position the stroller so Avi faces varied scenery and shade rather than the same canopy, giving his sharpening visual tracking new contrast and motion to follow.

content.todaysFocus: Anoushka's 6-week postpartum visit anchors the week. Expect exercise clearance for an uncomplicated delivery, a contraception discussion, and a final EPDS depression screen, while Avi's crying continues tapering off its peak.

actionItems.body: Attend the 6-week postpartum visit with written questions on pelvic floor symptoms, mood, return to exercise, contraception, and the return-to-work date. Noah should attend, since partner presence and support is the single most protective factor against postpartum depression.

Decide contraception at this visit. Progestin-only options, including the mini-pill, IUD, and implant, are compatible with breastfeeding, while combined estrogen products are usually deferred until weaning.
If Anoushka scores above 10 on the EPDS, ask for a referral today rather than waiting. Postpartum Support International keeps a directory of specialized therapists and a helpline.

watchFors: [low concern] Hair shedding starting around now and light yellowish-white lochia tapering off are both expected parts of recovery.
[monitor] Persistent low mood, loss of interest, or intrusive worry lasting beyond two weeks. Raise an EPDS above 10 with the OB; PPD most commonly presents weeks 2 through 8.
[call within 24h] For Anoushka, soaking more than one pad an hour for over two hours, a fever, or calf pain. For Avi, poor feeding plus lethargy plus decreased output together.

[call now] For Avi, a rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher, apnea, or blue lips. For Anoushka, thoughts of harming herself or the baby, or chest pain and shortness of breath. Call 988 or 911 now!

enrichment.body: Set up or refresh a high-contrast mobile so it stays novel as Avi's visual tracking sharpens. He now prefers faces and bold patterns and follows objects further across his field of view.
Place a baby-safe mirror at Avi's eye level during tummy time. Face-tracking is the strongest motivator for the head lifts that build toward steady head control.
Respond to each of Avi's coos as if he spoke, pause two to three seconds, then answer his next sound. These conversational turns, not raw word count, predict later language outcomes.

content.todaysFocus: Week 7 opens the last stretch before the 2-month visit. Crying is tapering, Avi's head is steadier when held upright, and tummy time is the lever for the forearm push-ups that come next.

actionItems.body: Build tummy time toward 30-45 minutes a day, spread across short bouts after feeds when Avi is alert. Adequate prone time reduces flat-head risk and supports on-time rolling and sitting.
Schedule the 2-month well visit in the next one to two weeks if it is not locked in, and start a feeding and output log to bring along.
If a 100-day photo session is planned, book the photographer now. The day-100 window falls around weeks 14-15, and good photographers book out weeks ahead.

watchFors: [low concern] Drool starting now reflects early salivary gland maturation, not necessarily teething, and brief rolling-eye episodes during sleep transitions are normal.

[monitor] A persistent head tilt to one side with limited rotation suggests torticollis, common after in-utero positioning. The pediatrician can refer to physical therapy at the 2-month visit if it is not resolving.
[call within 24h] Persistent vomiting beyond 24 hours, or refusal of several feeds in a row.
[call now] A rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher, lethargy out of proportion to recent activity, or bluish color around the lips. For blue lips or labored breathing, call 911 now!

enrichment.body: Encourage push-ups on the forearms during tummy time by setting a toy or open board book at his eye level. His head is steadier upright now, and prone propping builds the neck and shoulder strength behind it.
Dangle a simple toy within view and watch Avi look at it briefly and follow it with his eyes, the early visual tracking that precedes reaching.

Answer Avi's increasingly varied coos and gurgles with full turn-taking: respond, pause, then respond again to his next sound. Conversational turns predict later language-related brain function independent of total word count.

content.todaysFocus: Visually guided swiping is beginning: Avi is starting to look at an object and move his arm toward it. Week 7 keeps the focus on motor and sensory practice as nighttime stretches sometimes lengthen to 4-5 hours.

actionItems.body: Hold a lightweight toy within arm's reach and let Avi look at and bat toward it. Early swiping links his sharpening vision to arm movement and lays groundwork for deliberate reaching.
Keep tummy-time bouts short and frequent after feeds, aiming for 30-45 minutes cumulative. Distributing it across the day reduces protest while still building upper-body strength.
Continue Avi's 400 IU/day vitamin D, and keep him in shade rather than direct sun during any outdoor time.

watchFors: [low concern] Varied cooing and gurgling, and brief startles that settle quickly, are signs of an organizing nervous system this week.
[monitor] Movement that consistently favors one side, or a head that keeps turning to the same side, which can point to torticollis worth raising at the 2-month visit.
[call within 24h] Persistent vomiting past 24 hours, or refusal of multiple feeds in a row despite hunger cues.
[call now] A rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher in an infant under 3 months, blue color around the lips, or labored breathing. For blue lips or an unresponsive spell, call 911 now!

enrichment.body: Live-sing a clapping song, shifting tempo from slow to fast and back, to keep Avi's perceptual range wide while his ear for rhythm sharpens.
Lay Avi on a blanket on the grass in shade for a short window of outdoor light and varied texture, alternating with prone time on the blanket.
Offer a high-contrast object at arm's length and watch Avi fix on it and swipe. Pairing the visual target with the reach trains hand-eye coordination at its earliest stage.

content.todaysFocus: The nightly bath becomes a multisensory language lab this week. Slow narration of each step turns a routine task into concentrated language input, and a predictable wind-down anchors sleep-onset cues.

actionItems.body: Treat bath time as enrichment, narrating each step slowly: warm water, soap on his shoulders, lift the arm, splash. Continuous narration during awake-alert time is the right target for this age.
Name each body part and action as you go. Across 18-plus months of nightly baths, this adds up to enormous cumulative exposure, and conversational turns matter more than raw volume.
Confirm the 2-month visit is on the calendar within the day 56-70 window and keep the feeding and output log current to bring along.

watchFors: [low concern] Increased drool and brief eye-rolling at sleep transitions remain normal; the drool is salivary maturation, not early teething.
[monitor] No social smile in response to your face or voice yet. Many infants smile by now; note it for the 2-month visit if absent by 8 weeks.
[call within 24h] Persistent vomiting beyond 24 hours, or refusal of several feeds in a row.
[call now] A rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher under 3 months, blue color around the lips, or labored breathing. For blue lips or an unresponsive episode, call 911 now!

enrichment.body: Use the bath as a multisensory station: warm water, slow narration, and gentle skin contact give Avi coordinated touch, sound, and temperature input in one routine.
Read a short board book during the wind-down after the bath to pair settling with shared reading and start an early sleep-onset cue.
Pause after each narrated step and respond to any coo or movement Avi offers, keeping the serve-and-return cadence alive even before words.
